label: Churra

names.text: Taken from the English Wikipedia Churra sheep page: Churra Lebrijana (also called Atlantica or Marismeña), Churra Tensina, and Oveja Churra.

about.text: The Churra is a traditional triple-purpose sheep from the Duero Valley in Castile and León, north-western Spain, raised for milk, meat and wool. In Zamora province its milk is used to make Zamorano cheese.

sources.text: Origin, purposes and Zamorano cheese as stated on the English Wikipedia Churra sheep page.

origin.place: Duero Valley, Castile and León, north-western Spain

links.name: CIHEAM sheep and goat breed document

sources.text: Region of origin from the Wikipedia page; the CIHEAM document was seen only through WebSearch's text, which gives the Duero Valley and Castile and León as the breed's home. The Wikipedia page lists Spain and Portugal as countries of origin.
Described as a traditional triple-purpose breed, raised for milk, meat and wool. The wool is coarse and suited to carpet-making.
The page's infobox gives the conservation status as not at risk, citing DAD-IS (2023). The DAD-IS datasheet itself was not reachable.

facts.v: In Zamora province the breed's milk is used to make Zamorano cheese.

sources.text: Stated on the English Wikipedia Churra sheep page. The page does not mention a protected designation for the cheese.
